spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands from Kauai in the northwest to Hawaii Island in the southeast. Extensive bright white cumulus, stratocumulus and frontal clouds cover much of the northern and southern parts of the scene and partly obscure Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, Maui and northern Hawaii Island. Central waters are dark open ocean with scattered thin white cloud streaks. Around Hawaii Island there are bright white orographic and low clouds to the west and south of the island, but no distinct gray, brown or off-white haze or streak separate from ordinary meteorological cloud is visible emanating from the island.

classify.caveats: No plume found; nothing to classify.

kilauea.activity_summary: Lava flows began erupting from the north vent within Halema'uma'u yesterday, November 2, and are continuing this morning. High fountaining remains a possibility today or anytime within the next few days. Overview: Lava flows began yesterday, November 2, from the north vent in Halemaʻumaʻu and are continuing this morning.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
